quick: 0.5 mL IM per dose (pediatric schedule; select high-risk adults)

summary: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) conjugate vaccine is a polysaccharide-protein conjugate that induces protective antibody against Hib invasive disease (meningitis, epiglottitis, sepsis). It is given intramuscularly as a 0.5 mL dose in an infant primary series with a booster (schedule varies by product: PRP-OMP at 2 and 4 months; PRP-T at 2, 4, 6 months), plus a 12-15 month booster. Select older children/adults at high risk (asplenia, HIV, transplant) may receive it. It is well tolerated; serious reactions are rare.
indications: Routine active immunization of infants and children to prevent invasive disease caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b

Immunization of unvaccinated older children and certain high-risk adults (e.g., functional/anatomic asplenia, sickle cell disease, HIV infection, hematopoietic stem cell transplant, complement deficiency)

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at 2, 4 and 6 months of age
dosage.n: Number of primary doses is product-specific

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at 2 and 4 months of age
0.5 mL IM at 12-15 months of age
0.5 mL IM; number of doses depends on age at first dose

dosage.n: e.g., asplenia, HSCT, HIV; follow ACIP guidance

admin: Administer intramuscularly; anterolateral thigh in infants, deltoid in older children/adults
Do not inject intravenously, intradermally or subcutaneously (SC only if a bleeding disorder contraindicates IM)
Shake the vial/syringe to obtain a uniform suspension before injection
May be given concurrently with other routine childhood vaccines at separate sites
Observe the patient for syncope and immediate allergic reactions after injection
moa: The vaccine consists of the Hib capsular polysaccharide (polyribosylribitol phosphate, PRP) covalently conjugated to a carrier protein (e.g., tetanus toxoid or meningococcal outer membrane protein). Conjugation converts the T-independent polysaccharide into a T-dependent antigen, inducing robust, memory-based anticapsular antibody responses even in infants, conferring protection against invasive Hib disease.

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) to a previous dose or to any vaccine component
For tetanus-toxoid-conjugated products, known hypersensitivity to that component
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever (defer until recovery)
Age younger than 6 weeks (may induce immune tolerance to PRP)
History of Guillain-Barre after a prior conjugate (consider risk-benefit)

preg: Hib vaccine is not routinely indicated in pregnancy. As an inactivated conjugate vaccine it is not expected to harm the fetus; administer to a pregnant person only if clearly indicated (e.g., high-risk asplenia) and benefit justifies use.
lact: The vaccine is compatible with breastfeeding. Neither vaccination of the mother nor of the breastfed infant poses a risk related to lactation.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment. Patients on dialysis or with nephrotic syndrome may have high-risk indications for vaccination.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) - may reduce immune response
Combination vaccines - follow product-specific co-administration guidance
minor: Other vaccines - may be co-administered at separate injection sites
interactions.diagnostics: Recent receipt may transiently produce detectable urinary Hib polysaccharide antigen; interpret urine antigen tests for Hib cautiously after vaccination.

monitoring: Immediate post-vaccination observation for allergic reactions and syncope
Local injection-site reactions and fever in the days after
Completion of the full age-appropriate series
counsel: This vaccine protects against serious Hib infections like meningitis
Mild fever, fussiness and soreness or redness at the injection site are common and short-lived
Give the child paracetamol/acetaminophen if advised for fever or discomfort
Seek urgent care for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face/throat, or hives
Complete all scheduled doses for full protection
pk: Protective antibody develops about 1-2 weeks after dosing
Peak antibody response 2-4 weeks after the series/booster
Not applicable (vaccine, not a metabolized drug)
Long-lasting protection via immunologic memory after full series
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (35-46 F); do not freeze
pearls: Conjugation to a carrier protein makes the polysaccharide immunogenic in infants under 2 years
PRP-OMP product needs only 2 primary doses (2, 4 months); PRP-T needs 3 (2, 4, 6 months); all need a 12-15 month booster
Do not give before 6 weeks of age - early dosing can induce tolerance to PRP
Recent vaccination can transiently cause positive urine Hib antigen tests - do not mistake for infection
Indicated in high-risk adults (asplenia, HIV, HSCT, complement deficiency), not routine healthy adults
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, give it at the next opportunity and continue the series without restarting - the catch-up schedule depends on the child's age. There is no need to repeat earlier doses.
overdose: Overdose is highly unlikely. Inadvertent administration of an extra dose is not expected to cause harm beyond possibly increased local reaction; manage supportively.
